surfaces.part: cave ceiling band with hanging stalactites

answer.evidence: The object is a row of stalactites hanging from a ceiling edge, shown as a flat wall-mounted vertical face. The silhouette narrows steadily from 48 px wide at rows 0-1 to a point at row 14. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or contents that would indicate a horizontal top surface. The shading is only vertical faces with a darker right edge. It reads as a front elevation with no top surface, which is acceptable for a flat wall-mounted object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is four tiny, thin stalactite spikes with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. It shows roughly 3 tones (a light tan top, a mid-brown body and a dark tip or edge), where the bench, hedge, stall and well each show 5-6 steps. Shading is shallow, with little per-spike highlighting or rock grain. The dark edge pixels are 55% near-neutral, so the outline leans grey rather than a clear dark rock tone, and there is no clear tinted edge like the hedge's 0%. Texture is minimal: no speckle, no cracks, no clustered facets, so the spikes look like flat sticker shapes beside the richly textured well and stall. The per-tile facts are 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. By eye it is noticeably thinner and flatter than even the simple bench, and a careful artist would not accept it next to the references.

This is a flat wall-mounted face-on drawing. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no visible contents. The shading is vertical, with a lighter left side and a dark right edge on each spike. No horizontal top surface is drawn, so it reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of small stalactite spikes with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. Each spike shows about 2-3 lightness steps: a light top band, a mid body and a dark tip. The Beodeul references show 5-6 steps per material with per-element highlights, grain and clustering. The candidate has no visible tone count per tile because it is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. It looks thin and flat next to the hedge, well and stall, with no rock grain, facets or per-stone shading. The outline is partly neutral (55% near-neutral dark edge pixels) and partly tinted, so I call it mixed rather than a clear dark material tone. The 55% figure is above the well (33%) and bench (44%) references and below the lamp (100%), and by eye the dark edges read as grey-brown, not a clearly tinted rock tone. It is not flat-fill by the 5x5 measure only because the spikes are narrow. By eye the spikes are simple shapes with few tone changes, so the piece reads as shallow and sticker-like next to the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small row of four thin stalactite spikes with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. Each spike reads as about 2-3 tones (a light brownish body, a darker edge and a pointed tip), with no per-rock shading, highlight clusters, grain or speckle. The references (well, stall, hedge) show 5-6 steps with texture dots and clustered shading. 55% of the candidate's dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is partly a grey/dark line rather than a clearly tinted material tone.
